ROUND 2 - EMAIL FOUND. Affiliation re-confirmed from the raw PDF text of 2606.01879 (not the HTML): the title page reads '...XiayuCao1 ZihanZhang3 XiachongFeng2... 1 Harbin Institute of Technology 2 The University of Hong Kong 3 Harvard University', i.e. Harvard is superscript 3 (the earlier note said 2; the conclusion Harvard-not-HIT was right either way). Because the arXiv co-author graph is a stronger anchor than a name search for so common a name, I queried the arXiv API for au:"Zihan Zhang" AND au:"Bing Qin" and got two further papers beyond CultureForest, both from the same HIT-SCIR lab and both placing this Zihan Zhang at Harvard: (1) arXiv:2603.22862v2 'The Evolution of Tool Use in LLM Agents', whose title page prints 'ZIHAN ZHANG, Harvard University, USA' among HIT-SCIR co-authors and whose ACM contact block prints the one-to-one tuple 'ZihanZhang, Zihan_zhang@hsph.harvard.edu, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA, USA'; (2) arXiv:2605.09422 'Perception Without Engagement: Dissecting the Causal Discovery Deficit in LMMs', whose author block reads 'ZihanZhang5' with '5 Harvard University' alongside 1 Harbin Institute of Technology / 2 Pengcheng Laboratory / 3 NUS / 4 Peking University. The namesake test is therefore passed on three independent anchors at once - institution (Harvard University, and the address's hsph.harvard.edu = Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health is a Harvard domain), co-authors (Bing Qin, Jiafeng Liang, Runxuan Liu and the HIT-SCIR group recur across all three papers, exactly the group behind CultureForest), and topic (LLM/LMM evaluation and reasoning) - plus a self-identifying local part, 'Zihan_zhang'. The shift risk flagged for Chinese-group arXiv conversions does not apply: this came from the PDF, and the acmart contact block binds name, address and affiliation inside a single comma-separated tuple, which is the clean one-to-one mapping required for acceptance.
